994460482b693c096ff9718a1e1deb1190c10904: Minschuns is a small, modestly sized resort — 18 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and lift queues that barely exist. Minschuns' family reputation is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. With a summit at 2673 m and a village at 2126 m, Minschuns' snow reliability is generally dependable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can create tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly once the first serious snowfalls arrive. At 44€ the day lift pass places Minschuns in the mid-range category on budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Minschuns does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

Pizol's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-run childcare service, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Pizol's altitude (509 m at the bottom, 2250 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow cover in mid-winter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Pizol is clearly on the expensive side: a day lift pass costs 73€, and accommodation and mountain restaurants are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence, but be aware of it before you go. In short: Pizol doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It is an honest, often underrated destination that deserves to be (re)discovered.
